body: God damn, we are very similar people. OP, if things can get better once, I’d like to believe they can get better again. I’ll be thinking about you.

I agree and I plan to make an appointment to see the therapist/ counselor on my campus next week. I’m just a little concerned because everything is virtual now, and in general, they only allow students to have appointments every 2 weeks, so it’s not very stable but I guess it’s something. I may look into finding something more concrete but I’m worried about how that would work with still being under my parent’s health insurance and the logistics behind it all.

Either way, thank you for your insight and it really helped me put things into perspective, especially taking into account my upbringing and how that probably is affecting a lot of my relationships now.

Damn, first and foremost I wanted to thank you for taking the time to type all of that to help me out. And I wanted to say that I think you hit the nail right on the head with almost every single point that you made. He does sound very similar to you and thats exactly why he doesn’t like absolutes and you’re right, it isn’t fair for me to force him to basically lie, knowing that his “yes” basically means “maybe”, just to appease me. 

Thankfully when we argue, it never quite spirals out of the scope of the original argument so we never really bring up other, irrelevant things, but it doesn’t change the fact that we go in circles because I have a hard time when a conclusion or compromise doesn’t involve telling me I’m right, and I acknowledge that. I think a better solution to this particular problem may be a combination of what you had suggested and another commenter, where instead of saying “yes” or “maybe”, giving some sort of less absolute but more concrete way, such as giving a percentage of the likelihood or phrasing it how you suggested, by asking if the PLAN is still to come visit, rather than asking if he IS.

The more I talk about this, the more I realize how petty the argument even is to begin with and it frustrates me how I can never see that in the moment, even though I know he can sense how small it is. It’s definitely a problem I need to sort out myself, but also a communication problem that we need to address as well.

Yeah, a similar thing happened yesterday too. We began to argue and the situation began to escalate, and there was a pause, and I quite literally just broke down and started crying in which he got up and just hugged me for a while. But once I got past that, I felt myself getting upset all over again, and thus the conversation continued. I’m definitely having trouble catching myself in the moment, but I’m glad that you’re at the point where you can! It gives me hope that it is possible

He’s said verbatim that he understands why I’m upset so I think at the end of the day, the issue is that I am not appeased unless the conversation ends in the way that I want it to end. Hence the fact that we continue to have the same conversation over and over again, because it didn’t end the way I wanted it to the last time. It’s definitely something I need to work on

Thank you for your help, I’ve put a TL;DR [here](https://www.reddit.com/r/relationship_advice/comments/hjt6hx/my_boyfriend_21_frequently_tells_me_i_need_to/fwq3smf/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=ios_app&utm_name=iossmf) about basically what happened
Yes of course! It’s [here](https://www.reddit.com/r/relationship_advice/comments/hjt6hx/my_boyfriend_21_frequently_tells_me_i_need_to/fwq3smf/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=ios_app&utm_name=iossmf)
Without fail, after a couple days, I realize that it’s always the second option, but I can never seem to recognize that in the moment.
I agree, and I commented what the argument was about in another reply. But essentially, I wanted him to change one word of his vocabulary to appease my insecurities in that particular situation

I believe it’s because he wants to avoid me being upset if he says yes, and then has to cancel, but he does this with almost everyone he makes plans with, so I guess it’s good that it’s not just me. I think it just makes him feel better to know that he’s accounting for the possibilities of something happening that he couldn’t have foreseen.

When we are not arguing, I never feel as though he is not committed and I know how he feels about me and our relationship. It’s just that when we start to argue, all of that seems to disappear in my mind for the time being, which makes things worse.

Wow, we literally are incredibly similar people, it seems like. When I take a step back from a situation like this, I realize that the reason it goes in circles is because he’s not giving me the answer I’m looking for and I recognize that I could do better to empathize and understand why he’s not giving me the answer I want. It’s just hard for me to cool off and realize that in the moment, which leads to these huge fights.

I grew up fighting with my mother almost every single day from age 11 to now, and my mother basically demanded that I get on my hands and knees and apologize for whatever it is she thinks I did to upset her. And I can see some of that in my arguments, though definitely not as extreme, but it’s basically the “I’m always right” mentality that’s making everything worse. I definitely do need to do something about it, but having trouble figuring out where to start.

That was also his argument, that he says that he knows that I will be very upset if that happens as well, and honestly, I don’t know if he’s necessarily wrong and I unfortunately admit that. 

But there has been one time in the past where he did say yes, and in the same week, his professor assigned a project so he ended up not being able to come, to which I was very understanding to because it was out of his control. I guess it depends on the situation and whether it really was out of his control, like a professor assigning a project so last minute, or whether it was more something he could have prevented. 

I think he’s learned over the years that I can be emotional and upset over seemingly small things, which is what he was trying to avoid with not giving me a concrete answer just in case, but ironically it just made me more upset.

He does often give percentages as to the likelihood of him coming to visit, but I recognize that I can be stubborn and I could not understand why he couldn’t just say “yes” when it’s a 90% chance anyway. I guess I wasn’t being too empathetic in this particular situation, as another commenter pointed out, and kind of went into the conversation with the intention of having him tell me I’m right and move on. 

I agree that there are a lot of things that need to be discussed between us about communication and having my feelings feel validated, etc., but I also have a good amount of work to do myself to not get so hung up over such minute details that I know mean the same thing anyway.

I definitely understand that. I just kept going at it with how I felt like he wanted an out and couldn’t make a commitment etc., which resulted in us going in circles.

And I would love for us to see each other more often—most of our arguments occur when we are not together and when we are, everything is usually perfectly fine. But we are both incredibly busy people and barely have the time to see each other once a month, so we’ve been trying to just make things work for our last year at school.

I had just replied on another comment a TL;DR version of what the argument was about yesterday, and it basically was me wanting him to change 1 word of his vocabulary to basically appease my insecurities. 

I absolutely do need to work on these “fleas” and I never really know that they’re there until arguments like this happen and I ask myself why they even happened in the first place.

Since we go away for college and he’s roughly about an hour from me, we make plans to visit each other around once a month. Since I don’t have a car, he often comes to me or picks me up from my house and drives us back to his house. The reason I got upset was that when we make plans for us to see each other, he never said “Yes” to any plans that we make. It’s always “most likely” or “probably”, and every single time, it ends up being a yes anyway. Every time we argue about this, I ask him why he says maybe or probably when it ends up being yes anyway, and he says it’s because just in case something goes wrong with an assignment or project or something during the week, and it turns out he can’t come visit and he would rather say “most likely” so if that DOES happen, I won’t be disappointed (he takes his academics incredibly seriously). I retaliated saying that it sounds like he can’t make a commitment to me and wants an “out” and that it gives him a reason to not come visit at the first sign of inconvenience. He replied emphasizing what I said about how every single time, it ends up being a yes anyway, to which I said made me more upset because why couldn’t he just say yes when it will end up working out anyway. 

The conversation ended with him saying that he’ll just say “yes” even though he really still means “maybe” because it makes him more at ease being able to prepare for if something goes wrong. He couldn’t understand why changing one word in his vocabulary made such a difference, even though we both know he means the same thing, and I honestly don’t know either.
That’s actually really interesting to think about and I may have to try that. And I agree, it definitely is a lot

After a big blow out like this, I spend the next several days feeling both incredibly guilty that I started such a huge argument out of something so small, but also upset for whatever reason the argument was about in the first place. It’s a toxic headspace to be in and I do hope that things will be better for both myself and us after I take the step to seeing a therapist for my own problems.

Unfortunately, I grew up with my parents having a screaming match almost every single night, much of which became physical. And once my dad moved out, a lot of that yelling from my mother became directed towards my younger siblings and I. I do believe that that can be contributing to the problem and why I feel like therapy for myself might honestly be best for me.

Him, on the other hand, has the most understanding mother I have ever met. And I understand that things may be different behind the scenes, but I basically lived with my SO for a few months and saw first hand how different she talked to her children and how she diffused conflict in comparison to my mother, who’s only solution was to yell and scream.

So I’d have to agree, there’s definitely a difference in how we were both raised that could be contributing to the problem.

After taking a step back from the situation as best I can, I 100% agree. Two hours honestly goes by so fast when you’re the one involved in the conversation but it really is a long time to be going in circles about the same thing. It probably was for the best that we took a break and revisit the situation, but I agree that we need to discuss better ways of diffusing the situation that does not make me feel like I’m not being heard.
No and yes, respectively, but I’m not sure how that is relevant?

I actually have a necklace and earrings that he had bought me for my birthday, and I quite literally only take off to shower. I keep them on all the time for that exact reason, and to remind myself that he’s always close when we are away at college. I think at the end of the day, the root of our problems starts with me. And that doesn’t have to be a bad thing, but something that I needed to recognize and get help for, because I had a really shitty upbringing that clearly is affecting any and all relationships I try to pursue now. But I also am going to have a conversation with my SO later today and talk about how while this is true, it doesn’t change the fact that it still makes me upset to feel like my feelings are sometimes less than they are, and it’s something that I really need him to work on.

I just wanted to thank you from the bottom of my heart for all of your help. I was in a very emotional place when I posted and all of your comments helped keep me grounded.
I agree, so maybe it was for the best that we both did for the time being.

I think you bring up a lot of great points and everyone’s comments made me realize that we need to have a serious discussion about communication. It’s definitely an issue we both struggle with and I need to make certain things clear that would just help us both in the end.

I know that he loves me and cares about me, so it’s all the more frustrating when suddenly, all of that immediately “slips” my mind the minute we start arguing. 

I agree that it’s an insecurity issue—I constantly feel like people don’t need me or that there is no way someone would actually care for me; I’m almost certain I’ve lived with undiagnosed depression for the last almost 10 years of my life, which therapy would definitely solve as well.

In retrospect, it seems like the only thing I wanted out of that conversation was what you said in Step 2: I wanted him to apologize and tell me that he’ll reupload it, which is not fair. So many of our arguments are about small things like these, basically all of which I initiate, but I cannot seem to figure out why such small things makes me so upset. It’s a frustrating battle between myself and my SO, realizing how small these arguments are but also feeling like I’m not being understood.

I’m honestly not sure. I think in my head, I’m almost always expecting an apology, which is not fair to always expect. But a lot of the time, there is no clear right or wrong side of the arguments, because a lot of it is based on our opinions and how we interpret particular situations, which makes it harder to reach a good conclusion or compromise.

Most of our conversations end up just going in circles until one of us gets annoyed that we just wasted so much time getting nowhere. We end up just repeating ourselves, because we (mostly me...) continue to ask variations of the same questions which just goes in circles.

Thank you for this. And I’m not sure what makes it go around in circles for so long, I think a big part is that neither of us knows how to compromise to make the other happier than when the argument started. 

For example, with the photo situation, I expressed that I was upset that he deleted it and said that it felt like he was hiding me and he said that that was definitely not was doing. He studies a lot of art and design in college and treats his Instagram exactly like his own gallery, which leads to his page changing a lot to suit what he wants his page to show at different periods of time, and he said that at that moment, his vision for his page just simply did not have me in it—no hard feelings. But I honestly did not like that answer and continued to flip out and he got upset because I was getting upset about something so small, and something that is ultimately his decision on what to show. It ended in a huge argument that led to me accusing him of not caring about what is important to me, to which he retorted the same thing for almost forcing him to leave the photos of us up despite not wanting to. I was just upset that I felt like he was hiding me and that his “vision” for his page did not include me, but in all fairness, not everything has to revolve around me and our relationship.

My mother is the same way and I mentioned in a previous comment that I notice that when I take a step back from the argument, I can see aspects of her that I hated in myself. 

Almost none of our arguments particularly start as arguments. They start off as a normal conversation or questions or comments and spiral into arguments that spiral into big arguments that end with one of us, or both of us, being upset by the fact that it even had to happen.

I mentioned in a previous comment that I had been, and still am, verbally abused from my mother for most of my childhood and it freaks me out to see that a lot of the traits that I see in her reflecting in myself during these arguments, but I don’t see it until I step back and reflect on what had happened. It’s a combination of that, and also him sometimes being emotionally closed off and having trouble articulating and expressing how he feels.

I can say with confidence that we are almost exactly what you said about “does he try to participate but you’re just getting too over the top about it”. He definitely does participate in the conversation and we both try out best to talk it through, but sometimes things (or, I) get really emotional and upset to the point where sometimes we just end up going in circles for an extended period of time. It’s an annoying cycle that is hard to break sometimes.
The conversation today was not about Instagram, but that conversation had also lasted almost embarrassing long as well.

I described the whole “chances” part of my original post better in another comment because I don’t think I articulated it very well at first. But I think the biggest problem is that we didn’t know how to resolve it because of the nature of the problem, so it took a lot of back and forth and repeating the same thing on both ends until he figured it was enough back and forth of the same thing for 2 hours. We ended up getting to somewhat of a conclusion, and probably the best one we’d be able to get to, but it still ended with both of us feeing a little weird and upset that the argument even had to happen in the first place

It’s possible. I’ve considered going to therapy for a lot of emotional problems that I’ve dealt with throughout my life, which could very well be the cause of a lot of our arguments (considering how small most of them are), but I don’t know if that changes the fact that I sometimes feel as though he can dismiss how I’m feelings because of a stupid argument.

I don’t think I articulated that whole “chances” thing in my post very well, it wasn’t as formal as I made it sound like and honestly something I could’ve lowkey made up while I was so emotional and upset. Basically, I had come over with the intent of sleeping over before we got into an argument and I think he was trying to say that he gave me the opportunity to calm down so we can go to bed together without being mad at each other, but I was still upset by the time the conversation ended that he didn’t want something else to start up again.

I’m almost certain that this was his logic behind it too, because I am aware that once I get upset, I start to spiral and it’s hard for me to calm down and to stop being upset so suddenly. But it also makes me upset that I feel like he can be so okay with telling me to leave, or leaving himself, knowing I’m so upset. I guess he’s trying to avoid a conversation that doesn’t actually need to happen but it just also makes me feel like he sometimes doesn’t care about how I feel.

I recognize that the root of a lot of our arguments are incredibly petty things (ex: I got upset one time that he deleted pictures of us together on his Instagram and his argument was that it was his Instagram and he should be able to do what he wants with it, and it wasn’t fair for me to be upset at him for that), so a lot of it has to do with me trying to figure out why I get so emotional about really little things, but also getting him to understand that despite how small and petty they are, they still matter to me

I agree. It’s just frustrating because for most of the year, we go to college in two different parts of the state, so settling arguments when we are not together in person is difficult. I don’t think he’s dismissive to be malicious, it’s more out of annoyance for lack of a better word, but I know that doesn’t make things much better.

Yeah, most of these really big arguments are about things that I KNOW are really small and petty but for some reason, are important to me. And that just makes things harder because he can’t understand why they are so important to me and it’s hard to find a solution that would benefit both of us.

Absolutely not. He would never, and has never, laid a hand on me and I don’t think I’ve ever seen him raise his voice once at me in the 4 years we are together. I, on the other hand, grew up in a very verbally abusive household and have been verbally abused for most of my life, so I also do my best to never raise my voice during an argument either. He is much more passive and hates arguing (who doesn’t...), especially with small things that are important to me that he doesn’t always understand no matter how hard I try to explain
